source.title: The jamming transition as a paradigm to understand the loss landscape of deep neural networks
source.authors: M. Geiger; Stefano Spigler; Stéphane d'Ascoli; Levent Sagun; Marco Baity-Jesi; G. Biroli; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out accuracy for fully connected networks trained to fit natural MNIST labels, but does not test the random-label held-out comparison in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper studies fitting and loss landscapes. It reports one held-out accuracy result for natural MNIST labels; its other results concern fitting thresholds, depth, and loss-landscape properties, not the generalization measures named in V2–V8. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper measures fitting transitions and loss-landscape structure. Its natural-label MNIST accuracy does not establish V1's coexistence comparison: the random-data experiments use synthetic inputs, rather than randomizing labels on the natural-label task, and report no random-label held-out accuracy. It reports no width-dependent test-error curve or other comparison named in V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that a hypostatic jamming transition separates fitting and non-fitting regimes, explain avoidance of poor minima conditional on sufficient effective parameter sensitivity, and find little depth dependence of fitting capacity. They direct the generalization consequences to separate studies.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines jamming and fitting transitions with fully connected networks; its MNIST experiment uses binary even/odd labels, PCA-reduced inputs, hinge loss, and ADAM. It does not use the random-label held-out comparison described in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the location of the fitting transition has mild dependence on optimizer, batch size, and learning-rate schedule; it also reports a different unsatisfied-constraint density at transition for MNIST than for random data.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary even/odd MNIST classification using ten PCA components has reported generalization accuracy above 90% at the fitting transition for P ≥ 10⁴.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected networks can generalize above chance at the fitting threshold on PCA-reduced binary MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected networks fit synthetic random inputs with random binary labels; the required parameter count scales approximately linearly with sample count and depends little on depth. Natural MNIST requires fewer parameters to fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting capacity and the location of the interpolation threshold depend on data structure but little on depth in the tested fully connected networks.

record.problems: The held-out accuracy statement is limited to binary even/odd MNIST with the first 10 PCA components at the jamming transition. The text gives no uncertainty estimate or random-label held-out comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows retained. The paper's other reported results concern fitting thresholds, Hessian spectra, and gap distributions, rather than the held-out generalization measures named by the versions.

untested.parts: The same architecture and recipe fitting randomized labels on the natural task, together with natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance correlated with generalization gaps and compared with alternative measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Optimizer and batch-size sensitivity concern the fitting threshold, not comparative held-out performance. Hessian spectra are not the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization relationship in V7. Additional fitting and landscape findings are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare held-out performance on natural labels with held-out performance after fitting random labels; reports accuracy at the jamming transition for a binary even/odd MNIST task.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and held-out performance.
Large-batch training and held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: fully-connected network
rows.stage_stated: trained with hinge loss using ADAM; training duration and network size vary with the jamming-transition experiment
rows.operation_detail: Fit binary even/odd MNIST labels with hinge loss; evaluate generalization accuracy at the jamming transition.
rows.note: The text reports accuracy at the jamming transition for P ≥ 10⁴, but gives no natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.
rows.check: The reported accuracy above 90% is correctly extracted, but natural-label accuracy alone cannot establish V1's random-label memorization/generalization comparison. The original partial state incorrectly treats an untested comparison as an incompletely observed effect. Figure 10 plots fitting thresholds, not held-out accuracy; the accuracy statement appears in Section VII's prose.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Binary even/odd MNIST at the jamming transition, P ≥ 10⁴
reader_labels.reason: The trained networks fit the data at the transition and the reported generalization accuracy is above 90% (R1). This supports coexistence of fitting and above-chance generalization in this setting, without testing the random-label held-out comparison.
